headline: Indian equities tumble as rising crude oil prices, IT sell-off, and Fed decision weigh on sentiment

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Surging crude oil prices near $116 per barrel weigh heavily on domestic equities and the rupee.
Sharp losses in major IT stocks drag down the benchmark Sensex and Nifty.
Continued foreign portfolio investor (FPI) outflows dampening market sentiment.
Caution and uncertainty ahead of the upcoming US Federal Reserve interest rate decision.
whatHappening: Sensex and Nifty fell sharply, dropping significantly during today's trading session.
Jio Platforms made its stock market debut, ending 27% higher than its issue price.
Union Cabinet approved a 3% Dearness Allowance (DA) and Dearness Relief (DR) hike for central government employees and pensioners.
Elevated crude oil prices put pressure on the Indian rupee as traders await global cues.
summary:
Indian benchmark indices fell significantly as surging crude oil prices and IT sector weakness spooked investors ahead of the US Fed decision.
Foreign fund outflows and currency pressures added to market anxiety, keeping benchmark indices under pressure.
On stock-specific news, Jio Platforms surged 27% on its listing day while companies like Vedanta Aluminium and Goodluck reported declines in Q2 net profits.
